stem:
Kabir weighs $6$ tenths of a kilogram of flour on a kitchen scale marked in tenths and hundredths.

Which two claims correctly describe the same mass?

One or more options may be correct.

options.text: $6$ tenths of a kilogram is the same as $60$ hundredths of a kilogram.
$6$ tenths of a kilogram is the same as $6$ hundredths of a kilogram.
Ten hundredths make one tenth, so $6$ tenths equal $60$ hundredths of a kilogram.
$6$ tenths of a kilogram is the same as the printed digit $6$ on the scale dial.

teacher.key_rationale: Ten hundredths make one tenth, so 6 tenths regroup as 60 hundredths without changing the mass. Matching only the digit 6 as hundredths is term substitution. Grabbing the printed 6 is surface capture.
